title: Assembly Dataset for Contact Based tasks for Learning from Demonstration
finding: Read four complete HDF5 members of 34 listed, two complete tasks and two separate steps. Eight left/right raw F/T streams total 10,550 wrench rows. Pose, sensor topic and transformed chain wrench have different sample counts. No independent seating or continuity signal verified.

title: Fiber Optic Force Sensor Experiments for Suction and Finger Grippers
authors: Asociación de Investigación Metalúrgica del Noroeste (AIMEN)
finding: Read six files from three tactile patch tests. Six-axis wrist probe measurements have a sequential integer index and 242,777 rows in total. Optical test6 and test9 have 16 channels. Test3 optical HDF5 has an empty root; no shared timestamps for proving optical–wrench alignment.
rights: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Original source credited here. Only recalculated summaries and file identifiers are included.

title: Experimental Data on Robotic Adhesive Application and Joint Pressing
finding: The 301 pressing rows pair drive current percentage, estimated output torque, RPM and spindle displacement. Current-to-torque conversion is exact at the published precision. Radial pressure film and section images provide independent spatial evidence without a per-sample force reference.
rights: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Original source credited here. Only recalculated summaries and file identifiers are included.

title: Automotive click-events for sound detection dataset
authors: Ricardo Espinosa; Hiram Ponce; Sebastián Gutiérrez
finding: Full DataSet.csv has 68,768 rows with 213 numeric feature columns plus Class, and 62,277 distinct feature vectors. Columns 1–213 and class values 0/1 are the original schema. No audio waveforms, waveform timestamps, one-to-one clip map, wrist wrench, or electrical continuity channels appear in the file.

title: Tensile tests on PEEL and LAP hybrid self-pierce riveting joints with and without adhesive
finding: 17 displacement/time/force curves in two workbooks, 923,766 complete numeric triplets across four sheets. These destructive post-assembly tests provide a mechanical-strength comparison, with no paired joining-tool trace or time of original seating.
